title: Design an Elevator System
relevance: High — staple LLD / machine-coding question (campus + experienced); tests OOP modeling, Strategy/State, scheduling (LOOK/SCAN), and concurrency at Flipkart, Uber, Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Atlassian-style loops.
company_notes: Very common campus/machine-coding design+code round at Flipkart, Uber, Swiggy, Amazon new-grad, and Indian product cos (working LOOK + clean classes beat unfinished pattern zoos); experienced FAANG/Atlassian/Microsoft LLD probes concurrency, direction-aware stopping, and pluggable dispatch; among the top ~10 canonical LLD problems.

phases.goal: Clarify scope and lock functional/non-functional requirements plus scale assumptions before modeling.

must_hit.point: Distinguish two request kinds: hall call as (floor, direction UP|DOWN) vs cabin call as destination floor only, with different stopping rules.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States hall calls need direction and that an UP car must not pick a DOWN hall call on the way.

must_hit.point: Clarify simulation step()/tick() vs real-time threads, classic up/down hall buttons vs destination dispatch, and whether capacity/doors/emergency are in scope.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Asks which execution model and which features are in/out before designing.

must_hit.point: State typical FRs: N elevators, M floors; hall and cabin requests; assign a car; cars move/stop/reverse using LOOK; optional floor/cabin displays.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists N/M, both call types, LOOK motion, and optional displays.

must_hit.point: State NFRs: direction-aware stopping, no lost requests, thread-safe if concurrent, extensible dispatch strategy, testable without hardware.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Calls out correctness of direction, request retention, optional concurrency safety, and swappable dispatch.

must_hit.point: Call out of scope until asked: weight sensors, door timing FSMs, emergency/fire mode, destination-dispatch panels, multi-building banks.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly parks advanced real-building features unless the interviewer expands scope.

probes: What are the functional and non-functional requirements, and what will you leave out of scope for now?
Are we modeling a deterministic step() simulation or real threads per elevator?

hints.1: Start by separating hall calls from cabin destinations and asking what is in scope.
hints.2: Frame FRs around N elevators / M floors, LOOK motion, and assignment; NFRs around direction correctness and extensible dispatch.
hints.3: Say: hall=(floor,dir), cabin=destination; prefer step() unless asked for threads; park doors/emergency/destination-dispatch until asked.

phases.goal: Identify core domain objects, request types, and ownership of assignment vs motion.

must_hit.point: ElevatorController (dispatcher) assigns hall calls; each Elevator owns movement and its pending stops.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Splits dispatcher assignment from per-car stop serving.

must_hit.point: Model Request with floor and type (PICKUP_UP | PICKUP_DOWN | DESTINATION), with equals/hash on (floor, type) so UP≠DOWN hall at the same floor.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Typed requests, not bare floors, and UP/DOWN at one floor are distinct.

must_hit.point: Floors are usually ints, not classes, unless per-floor panels/displays are needed.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Avoids Floor classes unless panels/displays require them.

must_hit.point: Elevator tracks id, currentFloor, direction (UP|DOWN|IDLE), and separate upStops/downStops ordered structures.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions dual ordered stop sets plus floor/direction fields.

probes: What are the main entities and who owns hall-call assignment versus pending stops?
How do you represent an UP hall call versus a DOWN hall call on the same floor?

hints.1: Name controller, elevator, and request; decide what each owns.
hints.2: Controller assigns; elevator holds LOOK queues; requests are typed.
hints.3: Request(floor, PICKUP_UP|PICKUP_DOWN|DESTINATION); Elevator has upStops/downStops; floors stay ints unless panels need classes.

phases.goal: Sketch a Facade-friendly class structure with Strategy, optional State/Observer, and clear APIs.

must_hit.point: ElevatorController holds List<Elevator>, ElevatorSelectionStrategy, and APIs requestElevator(floor, dir), selectFloor(elevatorId, floor), and step().
must_hit.evidence_hint: Shows controller fields and the three main entry methods.

must_hit.point: ElevatorSelectionStrategy interface with concrete NearestElevatorStrategy / LeastBusyStrategy for swappable dispatch.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names a strategy interface and at least one concrete policy.

must_hit.point: Optional ElevatorState hierarchy (IdleState, MovingUpState, MovingDownState) and ElevatorObserver (HallDisplay, CabinDisplay) as plug points.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Maps motion to State objects and displays to Observer subscribers.

must_hit.point: Optional thin ElevatorSystem/Building Facade over the controller; Command for button presses is optional if a simple Request DTO suffices.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions Facade entry and does not force Command.

probes: Walk me through your class diagram and the public API.
Where do Strategy, State, and Observer show up in the design?

hints.1: Draw controller → elevators and a selection strategy interface.
hints.2: Add requestElevator/selectFloor/step; elevators expose addRequest and dual stop sets.
hints.3: Controller+Strategy for assign; Elevator+LOOK queues; State for Idle/MovingUp/MovingDown; Observer for displays; Facade optional.

phases.goal: Implement direction-aware LOOK serving, dispatch selection, and a deterministic simulation tick.

must_hit.point: LOOK default: keep serving pending stops in the current direction; reverse only when none remain ahead (unlike SCAN to shaft end or FIFO zigzag).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explains reverse-at-last-pending-request, not shaft end or FIFO order.

must_hit.point: Implement LOOK with two ordered structures (e.g. min-heap/TreeSet for UP, max-heap for DOWN); LOOK ops O(log F) per add/stop.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses dual ordered sets/heaps and cites O(log F) ops.

must_hit.point: Dispatch via selectElevator(elevators, request): prefer nearest car that is idle or already moving toward the caller; assignment O(E) per hall call.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes nearest compatible car and O(E) scan of elevators.

must_hit.point: Prefer deterministic step() that advances every car one floor; immediate-dispatch controller calls elevator.addRequest after selection.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Chooses step()/tick simulation and immediate assign into the chosen car.

must_hit.point: Cost for assignment should consider distance, directional compatibility, and pending-load—not closest-idle alone under bursty lobby traffic.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Warns nearest-idle stampede and adds load/direction to the score.

probes: How does your elevator decide when to reverse, and how are stops stored?
How do you pick which elevator serves a new hall call?

hints.1: Contrast FIFO, SCAN, and LOOK before coding motion.
hints.2: Dual ordered UP/DOWN sets; reverse when nothing ahead; strategy picks nearest compatible car.
hints.3: upStops min-ordered, downStops max-ordered; step() moves one floor; selectElevator scores distance+direction+load in O(E).

phases.goal: Show Open/Closed plug points for dispatch algorithms, motion modes, and displays without editing core controllers.

must_hit.point: Dispatch is Strategy so NearestElevator / LeastBusy / zoning can swap without editing the controller (OCP).
must_hit.evidence_hint: New selection policy is a new strategy class, controller unchanged.

must_hit.point: Elevator motion as State (or clean enum FSM): Idle ↔ MovingUp ↔ MovingDown (± DoorOpen / Maintenance) so transitions are not a giant switch.
must_hit.evidence_hint: State objects/enum handle mode-specific behavior and transitions.

must_hit.point: Displays via Observer: elevators publish floor/direction; hall/cabin displays subscribe; elevator must not new Display().
must_hit.evidence_hint: Elevator notifies observers and stays UI-unaware.

must_hit.point: Peak/scale extensions: zoning, express shafts, or destination-dispatch; fairness via wait-time aging so nearest-car does not starve far floors.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions zoning/destination-dispatch and aging/max-wait for fairness.

probes: How would you add a new dispatch policy or door/emergency behavior without rewriting the controller?
How do displays stay updated without the elevator knowing about UI classes?

hints.1: Name the three plug points: Strategy, State, Observer.
hints.3: New LeastBusyStrategy implements ElevatorSelectionStrategy; DoorOpen as ElevatorState; HallDisplay implements ElevatorObserver and subscribes.

phases.goal: Explain thread-per-elevator follow-ups and the shared-state synchronization hotspots.

must_hit.point: Experienced concurrency follow-up: one thread (or actor) per elevator plus thread-safe request queues.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Contrasts step() simulation with per-elevator threads/actors.

must_hit.point: Controller reading currentFloor/direction while cars mutate them needs volatile or locked getters.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Makes published floor/direction safely visible to the dispatcher.

must_hit.point: addRequest must be synchronized with the car’s consume loop; never share one mutable queue across cars without locking.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Syncs producer addRequest with consumer motion; per-car queues.

must_hit.point: Immediate assign is simpler; a global pending queue helps when every car is saturated or you want re-balancing—still needs locking if concurrent.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Compares immediate assign vs pull-from-global-queue under saturation.

probes: If each elevator runs on its own thread, what race conditions do you protect?
How does the dispatcher safely read a car’s floor and direction while it is moving?

hints.1: Simulation is default; threads appear as a follow-up—name what is shared.
hints.2: Protect stop queues and published floor/direction; no shared mutable stop set across cars.
hints.3: Per-elevator thread; synchronized addRequest with mover; volatile/locked getCurrentFloor/getDirection; private queues per car.

tradeoffs.strong_answer: FIFO wastes travel by zigzagging; SCAN overshoots empty shaft extremes; LOOK is the usual interview sweet spot—serve current direction then reverse at the last pending request, implemented with dual ordered sets.
Floor sets are simpler but can stop UP cars for DOWN hall calls; typed Request (PICKUP_UP/PICKUP_DOWN/DESTINATION) preserves passenger-facing direction correctness.
step()/tick is deterministic and interview-friendly; one thread/actor per elevator shows concurrency maturity but requires protected queues and safe publication of floor/direction.

tradeoffs.topic: Immediate assign vs global pending queue
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Immediate assign (controller picks a car and addRequest) is simpler; a global pending queue that idle cars pull from helps when all cars are busy or you want re-balancing.
Strategy swaps interchangeable algorithms (dispatch); State encapsulates behavior that changes with internal mode and often triggers the next transition.

gotchas.trap: Treating hall UP and hall DOWN on the same floor as one stop.
gotchas.correction: Treat as two request types; only stop when car direction matches (unless it is a destination).

gotchas.trap: Ignoring a new request that appears while the car is moving.
gotchas.correction: Under LOOK, if it is ahead in the current direction, stop for it; otherwise queue it for the reverse pass.

gotchas.trap: Nearest-only dispatch under a busy lobby causing starvation/ping-pong.
gotchas.correction: Use aging/max-wait, peak modes, zoning, or destination dispatch so far floors are not starved.

gotchas.trap: Assuming door timing, capacity, and emergency belong in the first pass.
gotchas.correction: Add DoorOpen state and capacity checks only if the interviewer expands scope; emergency overrides strategy (e.g. force ground) when asked.

gotchas.trap: Sharing one mutable stop queue across elevators or unsynchronized addRequest with the mover.
gotchas.correction: Give each car its own queue; synchronize addRequest with the consume loop; expose floor/direction via volatile or locked reads.
